11.ai_answer: The Pyramid of the Sun (Huaca del Sol) was the largest adobe structure in the pre-Columbian Americas and served as the political and administrative center of the Moche civilization in Peru (c. 100-800 CE). Its significance includes: (1) Political power - it functioned as the seat of Moche rulers and elite, demonstrating centralized authority; (2) Religious importance - the pyramid was used for ceremonial activities, including ritual sacrifices, connecting political power with divine authority; (3) Architectural achievement - constructed from an estimated 130 million adobe bricks, it showcased the Moche's organizational capacity and labor mobilization; (4) Economic hub - it served as a center for redistribution of goods and tribute collection; (5) Cultural identity - the structure reinforced Moche social hierarchy and cosmological beliefs, with its orientation and design reflecting their worldview.
